assessments.summary: Dengue cases in the US are peaking with a 533% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, reaching 57 cases per week as of late October 2026.
Measles cases in the US are peaking with a 232% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, reaching 223 cases per week as of late October 2026.
West Nile virus cases in the US are peaking with a 1762% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, reaching 98 cases per week as of late October 2026.
Global flu test positivity is at 9.1% for the week of late October 2026, up 10% from the previous month, with US hospital admissions rising 76% over the past month.
Legionnaires' disease cases in the US are rising with a 79% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, reaching 280 cases per week as of late October 2026.
Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo are ongoing with sustained transmission across 67 health zones, including 10,668 confirmed cases and 5,198 deaths as of late October 2026.
Mpox cases in the US are rising with a 47% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, reaching 41 cases per week as of late October 2026.
Malaria cases in the US are rising with a 59% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, reaching 38 cases per week as of late October 2026.
RSV activity is at baseline with a score of 52/100, showing a slight decrease in global test positivity but a rise in US hospitalizations compared to the previous month.
COVID-19 activity is at baseline with a score of 48/100, indicating a modest increase in US hospitalizations compared to the previous month while Wikipedia readership remains low.
Marburg virus disease activity is falling with a score of 48/100, as evidenced by a rise in Wikipedia readership compared to the past year.
Whooping cough activity is rising with a score of 48/100, showing a significant increase in US reported cases compared to the same period last year.
Chikungunya activity is at baseline with a score of 44/100, indicating a slight decrease in US reported cases compared to the previous eight months.
Norovirus activity is at baseline with a score of 42/100, as indicated by Wikipedia readership at the 33rd percentile of the past year.
Hepatitis A activity is at baseline with a score of 38/100, showing a slight increase in US reported cases compared to the previous eight months.
